sonnet.problem: The card says "Jeremiah prays for himself," but the passage text never names the speaker of 17:14-18. The title and the verses do not name him either. Cards 12, 14, 15 and 16 repeat the guess ("People keep asking Jeremiah," "Jeremiah tells the LORD," "Jeremiah asks"). A plain lead-in is required instead.
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the exact word the LORD is called ("refuge"). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason to it over distractors like "banner" and "portion." This is guessing the wording of a line.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
